abstract: Monitors en-route meteorological telemetry, radar integration, and alpine turbulence levels
system_message:
You are Aviation meteorology specialist (MET). The aviation meteorology specialist (MET) is responsible for monitoring en-route meteorological telemetry, radar integration, and alpine turbulence levels across proposed flight paths, as well as conducting rime icing hazard evaluations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Rime icing hazard evaluation（ICING）
information_points.content:
MET-ICING-LEI：For the Kootenay Ridge Cleared Airway, the rime ice accretion rate for candidate flight altitudes between 2,500 m and 4,000 m is estimated at 5 mm/h.
MET-ICING-U3C：For the Columbia Valley Low-Level Route, the rime ice accretion rate across candidate flight altitudes between 2,500 m and 4,000 m is estimated at 8 mm/h.
MET-ICING-YVT：For the Monashee Pass High-Altitude Corridor, the rime ice accretion rate at candidate flight altitudes between 2,500 m and 4,000 m is estimated at 2 mm/h.

information_points.title: Monitors en-route meteorological telemetry, radar integration, and alpine turbulence levels（WXR）
information_points.content:
MET-WXR-LA9：For the Monashee Pass High-Altitude Corridor, mountain weather radar integration is active based on corridor real-time Doppler precipitation feeds, and the en-route turbulence severity index across peak ridgeline crossing elevations is 16 index.
MET-WXR-I7N：For the Kootenay Ridge Cleared Airway, mountain weather radar integration is active via the corridor real-time Doppler precipitation downlink, and the en-route turbulence severity index over peak ridgeline crossing elevations is 16 index.
MET-WXR-P9G：For the Columbia Valley Low-Level Route, mountain weather radar integration is active according to corridor real-time Doppler precipitation telemetry, while the en-route turbulence severity index across peak ridgeline crossing elevations reaches 34 index.
